Subject: Question on microcall aggregation and pilot minimums

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising for our checkout chat flow. Before we move the pilot agreement over to procurement, the finance team asked a follow-up on billing behavior for very short interactions. Two specific asks: 1) We have lots of ~1-2 token heartbeats and sub-20 token microcalls from mobile devices (telemetry + short prompts). Do those count individually against the "per-call minimum" or can they be grouped? 2) For the 30-day pilot we discussed, can we cap the effective minimum so we don't get hit on the first week with lots of small calls?

We tried to map this to the guide you sent but couldn't find a clear rule about sliding windows or intra-session aggregation. Procurement would prefer something deterministic they can put in the PO.

Attaching a short sample of our traffic pattern (nova-usage-sample.csv). Appreciate a short note on how Redwood will meter these microcalls and any concession you can offer for pilot billing.

Best,

Subject: Re: Question on microcall aggregation and pilot minimums

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear traffic sample, that helps. Short answer up front: microcalls will be eligible for aggregation for minimum calculation using a one-hour sliding window for the pilot, subject to the pilot concession below. Full policy in production remains per-call minimums by default, but pilots can opt into the aggregation exemption.

Key points and proposed pilot concession (suggest this be written into the PO):
- Normal billing: each request is rounded up to the minimum quantum (our standard quantum is 32 tokens for streaming calls in your plan).
- Pilot concession: for the 30-day NovaPilot, Redwood will aggregate all requests from a single API key within a rolling one-hour window and compute the minimum against the sum of tokens in that window. Practically this means many 1–20 token microcalls are combined and will avoid separate 32-token minimum charges each.
- Aggregation boundaries: windows are aligned per-client API key with a slide; tokens contribute to every window that includes the request time for billing continuity.
- Rounding: after aggregation, total tokens are rounded up to the nearest 8-token billing quantum for the pilot (we usually round to 32, but we will reduce to 8 for pilot to avoid overcharging small volumes).
- Anti-abuse: aggregation is disabled if we detect synthetic or hammering patterns (sustained >100 requests/min for >10 minutes). We will notify the customer and share metrics before turning aggregation off.

We propose the following PO language to make this deterministic for procurement: "For the 30-day NovaPilot (DEAL-9482), Redwood will apply a one-hour rolling aggregation window per API key and an 8-token post-aggregation rounding quantum to determine minimum-billing units. Standard per-call minimums (32 tokens) resume at pilot end unless otherwise agreed in writing. Aggregation is subject to anti-abuse protections described in the Redwood Pilot SLA."

Camila / Neha — tagging you for any legal/ops flags on how to phrase anti-abuse and whether we need a usage threshold to revoke the concession automatically.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Question on microcall aggregation and pilot minimums

Asha — quick follow-up from ops/legal perspective. Two clarifications we should add to the PO to avoid ambiguity: 1) define the API key scope (e.g., sandbox vs production keys), and 2) provide clear metrics/notifications for when aggregation is disabled. Proposed addendum text below — feel free to copy into your PO: 

Addendum for PO: 
- Scope: Aggregation applies only to requests using the NovaRetail pilot API key(s) explicitly listed in the PO (sandbox and pilot production key IDs). Any other keys will be billed under standard per-call minimums.
- Notification & thresholds: Redwood will send an automated alert to billing@novaretail.com if a single key sustains >100 requests/min averaged over a 10-minute window. Aggregation will be suspended only after a 30-minute notice period to allow NovaRetail to remediate.

Also, for internal tracking — we recommend a per-account cap on the concession (e.g., up to 250k aggregated tokens/month at pilot rates), after which standard rounding rules apply. That protects Redwood from unexpected spikes in bursty telemetry. Asha — does that cap feel reasonable for your pilot? If not, tell us the expected monthly aggregated token budget and we'll model it.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
